title: Turbulence at the Correlation Scale as the Driver of Magnetic Reconnection: In Situ Observations and Kinetic Simulations
abstract: We study the statistical properties of magnetic reconnection using high-resolution in situ observations from the Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) Mission in the terrestrial magnetosheath and kinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. For the first time, using in situ observations, we find that the statistics of upstream reconnecting fields in a macroscopic turbulent plasma system are closely linked with the amplitude of turbulence at the correlation scales. These results are further confirmed with fully kinetic plasma turbulence simulations. Consequently, the average magnetic reconnection rates and associated heating rates, determined through the upstream fields, could become orders of magnitude higher than those predicted using the turbulence amplitude at the dissipation scale. We then use a simplified model of the heating of reconnection exhausts to estimate the ratio of this reconnection heating rate to the overall energy cascade rate due to turbulence. Estimates from the PIC simulations and the MMS observations yield a ratio on the order of $1/5$, indicating that direct reconnection heating is playing a substantial role in dissipating the turbulent fluctuations.
